Pending DoE's own copy (DoE I47 C2). RE-VENDOR: coordinator-content-repo.
description: Per-repo AUTHORED capability manifest — the surface each platform repo EMITS declaring the capabilities (stores, query surfaces, indexes, embed pipelines) it offers sibling repos, with a REAL consume seam per capability. This is the Tier-2 authored substrate (PM decision) that replaced the rejected Tier-1 heuristic (version_highlights[] + wiki keyword grep) — see docs/plans/2026-07-17-cross-repo-capability-lens.md § Mechanism selection. the engine repo's engine op READS this file verbatim per emitting repo and aggregates N instances into fleet-capability-index.schema.json; it is never inferred or greped. Decentralized, per-repo emission — mirrors the Fleet Producer Contract emission discipline of strategic-self-description.schema.json (docs/wiki/hook-best-practices/state-placement-law.md § Fleet Producer Contract): no repo emits into a shared consolidation point. An own-deliverable repo authors the manifest with `capabilities: []` to publish `shapes[]` alone.

host_repo.description: The emitting repo's name — the polarity field a consumer plan compares against its own repo (`host_repo == plan_repo`) to suppress a self-offer (F1c). Echoed on every entry in `capabilities[]` so a downstream aggregation (fleet-capability-index.schema.json) can carry the field per-entry without needing to re-join back to a manifest-level value.

generated_at.description: ISO timestamp this manifest instance was generated/authored — the freshness anchor (F2). Consumed by the fleet index's read-time TTL staleness rule (AC8) alongside `refresh_cadence`.

refresh_cadence.description: The emitting repo's declared refresh interval for this manifest (e.g. an ISO-8601 duration like "P7D", or a human cadence label the repo commits to). Read alongside `generated_at` by the engine's aggregation op and by the review SKILL's read-time TTL downgrade rule (AC8) — past this cadence, entries sourced from this manifest are downgraded to stale/unverified rather than trusted as live.

capabilities.description: The capabilities this repo offers siblings. May be empty for a repo that has not yet authored any capability entries.

shapes.description: OPTIONAL. Copy-out exemplar shapes this repo offers siblings (DR-201 shapeEntry). Absent on a manifest that publishes capabilities only.

shape_id.description: Stable identifier for this shape, unique within the emitting repo's manifest.

shape_label.description: Human-readable label; the string a copy-out offer quotes verbatim.

shape_summary.description: One-line summary of what the shape is and when to copy it.

exemplar_path.description: Repo-relative path of the exemplar in the owning repo.

copy_posture.description: Whether a consumer may copy the exemplar out directly or must ask the owning repo first.

maturity.description: Fail-closed reachability marker; same enum and semantics as capabilityEntry.maturity.

provenance.description: Same enum and semantics as capabilityEntry.provenance.

source_repo.description: The emitting repo: a non-polarity echo of the manifest-level `host_repo`, never compared for consume suppression.

capability_id.description: Stable identifier for this capability, unique within the emitting repo's manifest (e.g. "workstate-store"). Stays stable across manifest regenerations so consumers can track a capability across refreshes.

capability_class.description: Coarse structural class of the capability — the class the prior-art-checker's construction-vs-production predicate (F1a) matches a plan's proposed-artifact-class against. Domain-aware matching (F1b) additionally keys on `capability_label` + data domain, so same-class-different-domain constructions do not false-fire on class alone.

capability_label.description: Human-readable label for the capability, e.g. "workstate store". Paired with `capability_class` for the domain-aware match (F1b) — coarse class alone is not sufficient to fire an offer.

consume_seam.description: REAL, structured seam a consumer uses to consume this capability instead of rebuilding it — an MCP tool name, a CLI invocation, an import path, or an HTTP endpoint the emitting repo vouches for. Populatable because the manifest is AUTHORED (Tier-2), not inferred (Tier-1) — this is what resolves the Staff Engineer's F4 seam-precision gap by construction: an offer can now say "consume via <real seam>" rather than degrading to "(unconfirmed)".

maturity.description: Fail-closed reachability marker (AC9). `unverified` is the default when the emitting repo has not self-verified `consume_seam` is reachable — never assert `live` for an unconfirmed seam. `stale` marks an entry whose manifest has aged past its `refresh_cadence` (read-time TTL downgrade, AC8, applied by the review SKILL at C4 as well as settable at author-time). `absent` marks a capability the repo is declaring it does not offer (a tombstone), distinct from simply omitting the entry.

provenance.description: Three-value provenance marker reused from strategic-self-description-standard.md's model. `curated` = hand-authored editorial judgment (the expected value for a first hand-authored manifest instance, e.g. rag's). `generated` = machine-derived draft, not yet human-ratified. `asserted` = human-typed factual claim with no editorial judgment and no observable signal. `generated`/`asserted` fail closed HARDER on `maturity` than `curated` (AC9) — a consuming reader should weight a `curated` `live` claim more than a `generated` or `asserted` one.

host_repo.description: The offering repo — echoes the manifest-level `host_repo` on every entry so the field survives aggregation into fleet-capability-index.schema.json without a join back to manifest metadata. A missing `host_repo` here (or at the manifest level) breaks the mechanical `host_repo == plan_repo` polarity check (F1c) the prior-art-checker bucket depends on — this is why it is required at BOTH levels, not just once.
